notes:
I wasn't able to write these notes, because I couldn't read any of the sources.

My first try asked for seven commentary pages at once and was refused for exceeding the tool's usage limit. When I tried again with fewer pages, I had no tool calls left, so no page content came back. You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, so I've left this blank rather than filling it from memory.

If you start a new request, I'll fetch the pages one or a few at a time. This is the order I'd go in:

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:**
   - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/job-34/
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/job/34.htm
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/job/34.htm
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/job/34.htm
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/barnes/job/34.htm
   - preceptaustin.org's page on Job
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:**
   - Methodist: Wesley's Explanatory Notes (biblehub.com/commentaries/wesley/job/34.htm or wesley.nnu.edu)
   - Reformed and Baptist: articles on Elihu from ligonier.org, thegospelcoalition.org, desiringgod.org or gty.org
   - Lutheran and Pentecostal: lcms.org and enduringword.com, if they cover it
3. **Other views:**
   - Modern scholarship: the translator's notes at netbible.org/bible/Job+34 and anything on Elihu at bibleodyssey.org
   - Catholic: Gregory the Great's *Moralia on Job* on ccel.org or newadvent.org
   - Prosperity or word-of-faith teaching: gotquestions.org, if it discusses Job and Elihu

Splitting the work by sections (vv. 1–15, then 16–30, then 31–37) would also keep each step small enough to stay within the limits.
